Question 11(c) [4 marks]: EVO will increase their product warranty from 1 to 5 years. How do increased warranties impact the operations process?
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
EVO manufactures batteries and supplies these to electric vehicle producers internationally. Recently EVO has gained a reputation for late deliveries.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Provides detailed cause and effect of how increased warranties impact the operations process relevant to this business
3 marks: Provides cause and effect of how increased warranties impact the operations process relevant to this business
2 marks: Sketches in general terms how warranties impact the operations process, may or may not link to this business
1 marks: Makes a general statement about warranties and operations processes

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
Warranties are extra promises made by EVO about the quality of a product: how they will repair, replace or refund any defects in the batteries for a specified period after purchase. Increasing the warranty from 1 to 5 years signals a significant improvement in product quality and durability. One impact on the transformation process is the inputs: the materials used in the batteries will have to be of a higher quality to last an additional 4 years. In addition, the monitoring and controlling processes will need to ensure quality standards are maintained, to identify any defects and that the batteries are built to the new higher specifications. In both cases increased warranties have a significant impact on the transformation process of EVO and the performance objectives of quality, dependability and cost.
